strings.name: Marie Curie
strings.role: Physicist and chemist · Pioneer of radioactivity research
strings.summary: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw and pursued higher education and radioactivity research in Paris. With Pierre Curie, she discovered polonium and radium and advanced the isolation and measurement of radioactive substances. She received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911. During the First World War, she also helped organize mobile X-ray services for wounded soldiers.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Discovery of polonium and radium
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Discovered two new elements with Pierre Curie through research into the radioactivity of ores.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Nobel Prizes in two disciplines
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Received the physics prize in 1903 and the chemistry prize in 1911, making contributions across both fields.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Wartime medical applications
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Promoted mobile X-ray examinations, bringing radiological techniques to the treatment of the wounded.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in France
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died of illness in Passy, France. Her research and years of radiation exposure also became part of the history of science.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Organizes mobile X-ray services
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Arranged vehicles and equipment early in the First World War and took part in battlefield examinations with her daughter Irène.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the Nobel Prize in Chemistry
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Recognized for discovering polonium and radium, isolating radium and studying its properties and compounds.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Continues teaching at the University of Paris
strings.timeline.event-04.text: After Pierre’s accidental death, took over his chair and continued her research and teaching.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Earns a doctorate and the physics prize
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Completed her doctoral work in physics and shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Discovers polonium and radium
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Studied pitchblende with Pierre and announced evidence for the two new elements in succession.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Marries Pierre Curie
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Established a family together and gradually developed a close scientific partnership.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Goes to Paris to study
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Left Warsaw for Paris and began university studies in physics and mathematics.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Warsaw
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born Maria Skłodowska; later carried out research under the name Marie Curie.
